subject: Archaeology
title: Roman Concrete: The Secret Ingredient
description: A quick win: understand Roman Concrete: The Secret Ingredient.

hook.text: Modern concrete cracks in decades. Roman concrete has lasted 2,000 years — and scientists just figured out why.

buildup.text: Romans mixed volcanic ash with lime and seawater. The recipe created a chemical bond that modern concrete lacks.

discovery.text: In 2023, MIT researchers found that Roman concrete contains 'lime clasts' — chunks that self-heal when cracks form.

twist.text: When water seeps into a crack, it dissolves the lime clasts, which recrystallize and seal the crack automatically.

climax.text: Engineers are now trying to add self-healing properties to modern concrete using the Roman recipe.

punchline.text: Ancient Romans made self-healing concrete by accident.

quiz.question: What makes Roman concrete self-healing?
options: Bacteria in the mix produce minerals that fill gaps
Lime clasts dissolve and recrystallize when water enters cracks
Volcanic glass fibers flex and reconnect when stressed
